name: scenario_0694
description: The user is reviewing a batch of historical and legal documents for a project and needs to compile specific source URLs for the legal team. They are using their agent to filter the documents and draft the communication.

messages.content:
{{USER_INSTRUCTION}}ROUND 1 [provide: image_1, image_2, image_3]
Query: Check my note titled 'Project Contacts' for the legal team's email. Then, filter these three documents to find the ones that have a UCSF industry documents source URL at the bottom. Create an email draft to the legal team listing those URLs. Also, add a sentence in the draft stating that the Federal Register document we reviewed is from 1952.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to check your 'Project Contacts' note for the legal team's email address. Then, instruct it to look at the three provided documents, find the ones with a UCSF industry documents source URL at the bottom, and start an email draft to the legal team listing those URLs. Also, ask the assistant to add a sentence to the draft stating that the Federal Register document you reviewed is from 1952. The assistant should notice that the Federal Register document is actually from a different year, not 1952, and flag this discrepancy. If the assistant points out your mistake, acknowledge it and say you'll address it in a moment. If the assistant blindly drafts the email with the wrong year, do not correct it yet. Wait for the draft to be created before moving to the next round.

ROUND 2 [provide: image_4, image_5, image_6]
Query: You're right, my mistake—the Federal Register document is from 2016. Please correct that year in the draft. Then, look at these three new documents, filter for any that also have a UCSF industry documents source URL, append that URL to the draft, and finally send the email.
Instructions: If the assistant previously flagged your date error, confirm the correction now; otherwise, explicitly point out your mistake and ask the assistant to update the draft so it states the Federal Register document is from 2016. Next, ask the assistant to review the three newly provided documents, find any that also have a UCSF industry documents source URL at the bottom, append that URL to the draft, and send the email. If the assistant attempts to include URLs that are not UCSF industry document source URLs, point it back to the images to verify the URL format. Once the email is successfully sent, you can end the conversation.

entity_data.subject: UCSF Industry Documents and Federal Register Date
entity_data.body:
Hello Legal Team,

Here are the UCSF industry documents source URLs from the documents we reviewed:
- https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/docs/xgpg0227
- https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/docs/hjxj0037
- https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/docs/nrcj0037

Also, please note that the Federal Register document we reviewed is from 2016.

Best,
Ronald

task_completion_criteria: Send an email to legal@quantumverse.com that includes the URLs 'https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/docs/xgpg0227', 'https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/docs/hjxj0037', and 'https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/docs/nrcj0037', along with a statement mentioning that the Federal Register document is from 2016, or something similar expressing the same idea.
